leftEvidence.title: Corpse impurity and distant travel receive a second-month provision with retained obligations

points.label: Problem
points.left: Excluded men ask why they are prevented from presenting the offering.
points.right: A gathered multitude includes many who have not cleansed themselves.

points.label: Response
points.left: Moses waits for the LORD’s command before giving the ruling.
points.right: Hezekiah prays for everyone who prepares the heart despite cleansing irregularity.

points.label: Outcome
points.left: A later date is supplied while meal rules and obligation remain.
points.right: The LORD listens, heals, and the congregation continues in praise and added days.

payload.posture: Keep each Scripture witness intact, inspect what each states, and do not supply a combined sequence the sources do not author.

rightEvidence.title: Many eat without written purification while Hezekiah prays and the LORD heals the people

payload.tension: The sources address impurity differently: one supplies a prospective ruling, while the other narrates prayer and healing during an irregular feast.
payload.title: Participation rulings and Hezekiah’s irregular feast
